subject: oceanography

resources.title: National Ocean Service Education
resources.notes: NOAA independent-learner tutorials and standards-aligned education resources spanning ocean, coasts and climate; useful for legitimate foundation/beginner coverage without mapping graduate material downward.

resources.title: NOAA Ocean Service Education: For Students
resources.notes: Student-facing tutorials include corals, coastal pollution, tides, ocean currents and estuaries.

resources.title: Introduction to Ocean Science and Engineering
resources.notes: Ocean systems and engineering course with freely available physical-oceanography reading, seafloor, measurements, atmospheric forcing, wind and heat topics.

resources.title: Introduction to Observational Physical Oceanography
resources.notes: Graduate physical-oceanography curriculum covering seawater properties, measurements, rotation, Ekman dynamics, wind-driven and thermohaline circulation, tides and waves, with problem sets and observational data.

resources.title: Evolution of Physical Oceanography
resources.notes: Graduate open-textbook resource covering general circulation, mixing, internal waves, variability, biological oceanography and other foundational physical-oceanography research topics.

resources.title: World Ocean Database
resources.provider: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information
resources.notes: Quality-controlled global ocean profile data; retain dataset/version/platform provenance.

resources.title: Tides and Currents
resources.provider: NOAA Center for Operational Oceanographic Products and Services
resources.notes: Authoritative U.S. coastal water-level, current and meteorological observations.

resources.title: Physical Oceanography Distributed Active Archive Center
resources.notes: NASA archive for satellite and model-based physical oceanography data.

resources.title: Coastal and Marine Hazards and Resources Program
resources.notes: Authoritative coastal geology, hazards, mapping and monitoring resources.

known_gaps: Dedicated chemical and biological oceanography curricula remain thinner than physical oceanography and should not be inferred from broad datasets alone.
Deep-sea ecology, marine biogeochemistry and specialist modeling need stronger exact-cell course coverage where the audit still reports gaps.
Research databases and observational portals do not establish expert readiness without item-level evidence review, runtime retrieval, provenance and applied assessment.
